scope_findings.claim: MAESTRO addresses next-generation AI agent architectures powered by large AI language models that can plan, utilise tools, and perform actions autonomously to achieve specified goals based on high-level instructions.

MAESTRO develops a hybrid neuro-symbolic planning engine that decomposes high-level goals into executable sub-task graphs with formally specified pre-conditions, post-conditions, and verification checkpoints, integrating search-based planning algorithms with LLM-driven heuristic evaluation.
MAESTRO supports self-correction through plan monitoring — detecting execution failures and replanning from verified intermediate states rather than restarting from scratch.

MAESTRO designs a unified memory architecture integrating working memory, episodic memory, and semantic memory, with a memory controller managing information flow between stores to sustain coherent long-term agent behaviour.

MAESTRO develops an External Tool and API Orchestration Layer providing a typed tool registry, formal tool selection and invocation policies, standardised API adapters, post-invocation verification, execution monitoring with fallback/recovery, and auditable tool execution traces.

MAESTRO develops multi-agent coordination protocols enabling heterogeneous agents to collaborate on shared objectives, including formal task-delegation protocols with provable convergence, conflict resolution mechanisms, and auditable multi-agent interaction traces.
MAESTRO incorporates qualitative and quantitative KPIs, standardised benchmarking across all demonstrators, and structured progress monitoring at 6-month integration checkpoints.
MAESTRO will build on publicly available results from relevant prior EU-funded actions including Horizon 2020 ICT-48 projects, ADRA partnership pilot projects, and Horizon Europe Cluster 4 actions.

All research outputs — frameworks, models, benchmarks, the External Tool and API Orchestration Layer, and demonstrator results — will be shared with the European R&D community through the AI-on-demand platform.
The project will link to the resources offered by AI Factories and Data Labs for compute-intensive training and evaluation.
Demonstrator results will be validated in Testing and Experiment Facilities and disseminated via European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs).

MAESTRO implements the co-programmed European Partnership on AI, Data and Robotics (ADRA) and will allocate dedicated tasks for cohesion activities with ADRA and the GenAI4EU central Hub (CSA HORIZON-CL4-2025-03-HUMAN-18).
MAESTRO will build synergies with EuroHPC Joint Undertaking, national AI strategies, ongoing Horizon Europe Cluster 4 projects, and the OECD AI Policy Observatory.

MAESTRO validates in two call-identified Apply AI sectors: healthcare (clinical decision support) and advanced manufacturing (process optimisation), plus a cross-sector logistics and supply chain transfer demonstrator.
scope_findings.flag_reason: SR-13 and CC-11 require portfolio coverage ensuring at least one proposal per each of the three sectors: healthcare, advanced manufacturing, and in-vehicle autonomous driving. MAESTRO directly validates in healthcare and advanced manufacturing but explicitly does not include in-vehicle autonomous driving as a demonstrator sector, citing absence of automotive sector partners. The concept note acknowledges this gap and proposes only an architectural mapping analysis (WP8) for autonomous driving transferability. Whether this satisfies the portfolio coverage requirement depends on evaluator interpretation: MAESTRO may be funded under the healthcare or advanced manufacturing portfolio slot, but cannot independently satisfy the in-vehicle autonomous driving portfolio slot. The concept's strategic positioning is honest about this limitation, but the claim that MAESTRO addresses the call's sector coverage requirements is only partially supported by Tier 2B scope data. Flagged for resolution: the concept should clarify which portfolio slot MAESTRO is targeting and confirm it does not claim to satisfy the in-vehicle autonomous driving portfolio requirement.

scope_findings.claim: Research activities start at TRL 2 and progress to TRL 5 across two call-identified Apply AI sectors plus a transfer sector, spanning the full TRL 2–5 range required by the call.
MAESTRO requests EUR 19,000,000 EU contribution over 48 months with 8 consortium partners.
All consortium partners are established in EU Member States (DE, FR, NL, IT, SE, FI, ES) or Horizon Europe Associated Countries (CH), satisfying geographic eligibility restrictions EC-01 and EC-02.
MAESTRO contributes to the Apply AI Strategy by advancing foundational capabilities for trustworthy AI deployment in key European economic sectors.
The concept note references advancing multimodal reasoning capabilities as a potential research area within the scope of the call.
scope_findings.flag_reason: SR-05 lists advancing multimodal reasoning capabilities as a potential (non-mandatory) research area. However, the MAESTRO concept note does not explicitly develop multimodal reasoning as a named research pillar or deliverable — it is referenced only implicitly through the broader agent architecture. The concept does not claim multimodal reasoning as a primary contribution, so this is not an out-of-scope claim, but the absence of explicit multimodal reasoning content means this optional scope element is not addressed. Flagged as informational: if the concept intends to claim coverage of this optional scope area, explicit content should be added; if not, no action required.

scope_findings.claim: The logistics and supply chain demonstrator validates the generalisability and portability of the MAESTRO architecture beyond the call's specifically identified Apply AI sectors, and the concept asserts this demonstrates cross-sector transferability to in-vehicle autonomous driving through an architectural mapping analysis.
scope_findings.flag_reason: The concept claims that an architectural mapping analysis (WP8) assessing transferability to in-vehicle autonomous driving satisfies the call's portfolio coverage logic for that sector. SR-13 and CC-11 specify that portfolio coverage requires at least one proposal focusing on each sector, subject to passing evaluation thresholds. An architectural mapping analysis is not equivalent to a demonstrator or direct sector focus. The concept's own strategic positioning acknowledges MAESTRO does not address in-vehicle autonomous driving as a demonstrator sector. This claim is borderline: it may be acceptable as a contribution to the in-vehicle autonomous driving portfolio slot if evaluators accept architectural transferability analysis as sufficient focus, but this is not confirmed by Tier 2B scope data. Flagged for resolution: the concept should not represent the WP8 architectural mapping as satisfying the in-vehicle autonomous driving portfolio coverage requirement unless Tier 2B source data confirms that transferability analysis is an acceptable form of sector focus.
